canonPolicy.rule: Regression fixtures test whether implementations preserve distinct transit-family mathematics. They do not establish setting history, canonical speeds, ranges, constants, or race-specific doctrine. Specific surviving race, organization, manufacturer, and named-technology sources outrank these fixtures.

gravitic systems have few strong natural planes

environments.name: Close Stellar Passage

expectedDiscriminators: metric burden rises

environments.name: Binary Saddle and Fork

environments.name: Compact Object Neighborhood
environments.purpose: test extreme curvature, tides and rapidly changing admissibility
expectedDiscriminators: many low-tier exotic solutions become NO-GO

environments.name: Dense Fleet and Artificial Gravity Field

environments.name: Severe Q-Weather
environments.purpose: test rapidly varying Q-state and shear conditions

environments.name: Reference-Poor Frontier

environments.name: Prepared Beacon Corridor

regressionInvariants.assertion: A favorable broad gravity gradient may reduce gravitic-plane route cost while increasing metric-envelope field burden; implementations that apply the same gravity penalty to both families fail regression.
Severe Q-weather must materially degrade slipstream-shear and Q-lattice solutions, while unrelated families receive no identical penalty without an explicit authority-backed coupling.
Reference-poor frontier conditions disproportionately penalize fold-jump, q-lattice and phase-displacement because endpoint/address/state authenticity is part of their solved problem.
High occupancy must strongly affect fold-jump and phase-displacement endpoint admissibility and gate traffic, but may not be treated as a universal FTL efficiency scalar.
Compact-object conditions may produce NO-GO outcomes at low maturity; a generator must not force every family to return a usable route.
Prepared beacon infrastructure may lower u_r, p_fork or endpoint/address uncertainty but cannot silently increase structural margin, field efficiency or power unless that mechanism is documented.
Wormhole-gate transit in a mature corridor optimizes aperture stability, synchronization, queue and throughput rather than shipboard FTL cruise speed.
Inertial-torch remains continuous causal propulsion and must retain ordinary trajectory distance, relativistic mechanics, propellant/power and thermal constraints.

Tier improvement must change an identifiable mathematical capability and be enabled by machinery, material, structure, energy, navigation, control or infrastructure development; unexplained scalar speed multipliers fail regression.
Every family must expose a family-specific abort/no-abort boundary; discrete commits and continuous recoverable transit may not share one generic emergency-stop model.

generatorRules: Evaluate every candidate family against the same environment snapshot before comparison.
Use the family response function and optimization target; never collapse the environment into one universal FTL difficulty number.
Resolve technology basis, race/organization/manufacturer authority and Path/maturity before choosing machinery embodiment.
When a fixture conflicts with surviving named canon, named canon wins and the fixture is adjusted rather than the canon.
Allow HOLD, DETOUR, INFRASTRUCTURE_REQUIRED and NO_GO results; generation is not required to manufacture a safe route.
Record which environmental term caused every route rejection, abort decision or performance reduction.
Record which mathematical capability and physical enabler allow a higher tier to overcome a lower-tier limit.
Do not promote numeric fixture values or thresholds to canon through repeated generated use.

The legacy 'different lightspeed methods' design source governs the requirement for method-specific gravity/topology/miscalculation consequences; its exact repository path remains UNRESOLVED until recovered.
